collection.description: A villager has decided to learn to juggle with three coconuts: keep practicing, or switch to something softer.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) has decided to learn to juggle. Nobody needs a villager who can juggle. It won't help with the harvest or fix a roof. (name1) wants to do it anyway. (He/She) has been practicing with three coconuts for a week, and has so far managed to catch none of them twice in a row.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (name1) practices every evening. (He/She) drops coconuts on (his/her) toes, on the grass, once on a passing chicken, who is fine but furious. Then, one evening, suddenly, (he/she) keeps all three in the air for a count of ten. (He/She) shrieks, drops all three, and doesn't care in the slightest.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: After one too many coconuts on the toe, (name1) switches to three bundles of rolled-up leaves. They're much easier to catch. They also look much sillier. (name1) doesn't mind. By the end of the week (he/she) can juggle the leaf bundles while walking, and the children follow (him/her) about asking for shows.
